keys.explanation: Controls must not compromise safe working light or life-safety egress illumination design.
CO2 is common for electrical/B hazards with low residue; still short range and asphyxiation risk in pits.
Layered controls (perimeter → envelope → zones → cabinets → process) assume single-layer failure.
Interlocked chambers stop unauthorized persons following authorized staff through one door.
Understructure type changes lateral stability, access patterns, and structural behaviour.
Actionable alerts beat naked point names during incidents.

30134-6 is ERF (Energy Reuse Factor). ERE is not that part. The series has more than three letters; this course names the distinction and stops. No single PUE target as law. Sustainability-track depth is not this leftover.
Rolling loads cover carts, dollies, and wheeled gear moving over the access floor.
For water-dependent designs, water is a first-class availability input like power.
Ownership and SLA boundaries differ by model, but both require engineered facility resilience.
Process and people failures (changes, procedures, maintenance) are major drivers of facility downtime.
Physical shared responsibility: customer zones vs provider common plant separation.
International standards are tools for alignment; adoption remains a national/project decision.
When climate and design allow, stored winter cold can offset summer cooling energy—site-specific engineering, not universal.
Teaching path: utility/generator → transfer → UPS → distribution/PDU → rack.
Horizontal segments serve the equipment zone from HDA or ZDA-type distribution points.
Cleaning is controlled work near electronics—technique matters.
Warmer operation within guidance can expand economizer opportunity and plant efficiency.
Liquid-ready is a cabinet SKU, not a denser air box. 800 mm, RDHx door, drip, CDU landing, and 40–100 kW structure are the frame questions. Liquid families live in Module 09. 19″ rails stay.
Water balance anomalies are early warnings for plant risk—instrumentation supports response.
Emergency lighting is for life safety and egress visibility under power loss.
MPO connectors enable dense multi-fiber trunks and cassettes common in modern DC backbones.
Growth without pathway and media planning creates congestion, risk, and unmanageable MACs.

HSE's permits-to-work guidance states that before equipment or machinery is put back into service, it will require a declaration from the permit originator that it is ready for normal use. That is the hand-back step, and it is a property of the permit, not of the work being finished: 'the job is done' and 'the plant may be returned to service' are two different authorisations. An escort signature (A) records site access, not plant condition — an escort never replaces a permit. A contractor sign-off (C) is the party carrying out the work declaring their own completion, which is not the originator's declaration. A verbal all-clear (D) leaves no documented declaration at all, and the permit is a documented procedure by definition.
Isolation is galvanic separation; still need proper UPS, grounding, and distribution design.
Monitor the chains and the monitors—blind spots include dead sensors and capacity blindness.
Circuiting and emergency transfer must match the life-safety design, not ad-hoc plug strips.
MTTR is maintainability/ops speed; spares and MOPs often dominate more than the part itself.

This file owns the fire playbook. 855 is installation; 9540A is test data, not a listing. Room vs yard is off-gas/deflagration vs next-enclosure. Interconnect stays in Module 06. No invented fire percent or agent mass.
Infrastructure failures are correlated across workloads; governance cares about systemic facility risk.
Signage supports life safety: evacuate-on-alarm messaging, agent type, and control locations.
BTM is how the hall energizes, not a genset you tack on later. Point at Module 01 for the noun and Module 06 for the path. Do not steal UPS/ATS/generator internals.

The M06 drawing distinction is a dedicated reserve plus catcher transfer path versus spare capacity spread across active blocks. TIA-942-C and Uptime's 2018 Tier Standard require the reviewer to reason from actual infrastructure topology and distribution paths; a catcher label is not a Tier, Rated, or Availability Class claim.
Outdoor climate drives HVAC sizing and free-cooling opportunity.
Adjacency to plant brings B-field, thermal, and operational traffic issues.
Keep health exposure language separate from IEC 61000-class equipment immunity.
Guides recommend practice; binding force comes from adoption into law, contract, or policy.
Equipment thermal limits are driven by inlet conditions at the hardware.

Analyze the frame, not the coolant name. A 600 mm air BOM cannot dress hoses, land an RDHx door, or carry 40–100 kW. CDU landing is reserved now. Blanking stays for air-cooled network. Immersion is not a 19″ frame.
DCIM ties inventory, power capacity, and change workflows to facilities data—not just environment sensing.
